It accesses local cache files and updates them conditionally by fetching new data via an abstract async method. There is no evidence of obfuscated code execution, subprocess spawning, credential harvesting, encryption of user files, or any other suspicious or malicious behavior seen in the known malware patterns. The code uses standard libraries and patterns for data handling and caching, with no attempts to evade detection or exfiltrate data. The obfuscation of variable names appears to be a code obfuscation or minimization technique but does not itself indicate malicious intent. Compared to the known malicious patterns, this code lacks key indicators such as subprocess spawning, session token theft, or ransomware-like file encryption.

slice_results.behavior_summary: When called, the code accesses and modifies local filesystem files using aiofiles and pathlib APIs to asynchronously read and write serialized pandas DataFrame objects with joblib compression. This behavior facilitates local persistent storage and update of structured data, with no network or process execution involved, thus primarily impacting local data integrity and persistence.
slice_results.explanation: [LLM Judgment: Benign] The analyzed code performs asynchronous reading and writing of pandas DataFrame objects to local cache files using joblib serialization with compression. It includes data integrity checks and logging/warning on data mismatches. There is no evidence of network communication, process execution, credential harvesting, encryption of user files, or obfuscation. The code's behavior is consistent with legitimate local data persistence and cache management. Compared to the known malicious patterns, it lacks any indicators such as exfiltration, encrypted payload execution, or ransomware-like file encryption. The obfuscated variable names appear to be a style choice rather than an attempt to hide malicious intent.

package_info.why_malicious: 8base ransomware is a financially motivated malware family that encrypts and exfiltrates user files, demands ransom for decryption, and threatens to leak stolen data. It employs process termination to maximize file encryption, selectively targets user files while avoiding system-critical files, uses anti-forensics techniques, and is distributed via malware loaders such as SmokeLoader. Its primary objective is extortion through data encryption and data leak threats.

attack_chain.action: Initial infection via SmokeLoader or other loader
attack_chain.leads_to: Ransomware execution

attack_chain.action: Ransomware process starts, scans for files and folders to target/exclude
attack_chain.leads_to: Process termination

attack_chain.action: Kills processes to unlock files for encryption
attack_chain.leads_to: File encryption

attack_chain.action: Encrypts files (full or partial based on size), injects null bytes, adds metadata
attack_chain.leads_to: File renaming

attack_chain.action: Renames encrypted files to include victim ID and attacker email
attack_chain.leads_to: Ransom note drop

attack_chain.action: Drops ransom notes in affected directories
attack_chain.leads_to: Data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Exfiltrates stolen files to public file sharing services
attack_chain.leads_to: Extortion and data leak

behavioral_signatures: Bulk termination of processes associated with productivity and database applications prior to file encryption
Selective exclusion of system-critical files and directories during file enumeration
Conditional full or partial file encryption with null byte injection and metadata tampering
File renaming to include .id[unique_id].[attacker_email].8base extension
Creation of ransom notes (info.hta and info.txt) in user-accessible directories
Outbound network connections to public file sharing services (Gofile, Pixeldrain, files.dp.ua, AnonFiles, Anonym File, Mega) following file encryption
file_indicators: Files with extension pattern: .id[unique_id].[attacker_email].8base
Presence of info.hta and info.txt ransom notes in affected directories
Exclusion of files/folders: ntldr, ntdetect.com, io.sys, recov, C:\Windows, C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows\Caches
network_indicators: Outbound connections to domains: gofile.io, pixeldrain.com, files.dp.ua, anonfiles.com, anonymfile.com, mega.nz
Network activity involving bulk file uploads to public file sharing services after file encryption
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for bulk process termination events targeting office and database applications, mass file renaming with .id[unique_id].[attacker_email].8base extensions, and creation of info.hta/info.txt ransom notes in user directories. Detect outbound connections to known file sharing services (gofile.io, pixeldrain.com, files.dp.ua, anonfiles.com, anonymfile.com, mega.nz) following suspicious file operations. Correlate these behaviors for high-confidence detection of 8base ransomware activity.
